bug_semantics: CWE-1321 prototype pollution in multipart/form-data parsing only. AdonisJS BodyParser feeds attacker-controlled multipart field names into FormFields.add(), which does lodash.set/get on a plain object store (`this._fields = {}` originally; later `#fields: any = {}`) without rejecting reserved keys. A field such as `__proto__.polluted` or `constructor.prototype.polluted` therefore writes onto Object.prototype at runtime. The sink at the patched versions is Multipart.#handleField(key, value) → FormFields.add(key, value) (and file fieldName via the same class). JSON and application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies use other parsers (qs/co-body) and are out of scope. Impact is unexpected behavior, logic bypass, or further issues depending on how polluted prototypes are later consumed. Affected: @adonisjs/bodyparser <= 10.1.2 and 11.0.0-next.0 .. 11.0.0-next.8. Patched by switching the store to Object.create(null) in 10.1.3 and 11.0.0-next.9.
flaw_origin: The flawed mechanism was first written on 2017-05-25 in 436bb11c1f78e2c8e3465284713006962ca255f9 (`feat(*): implement body parser`) as src/FormFields/index.js: constructor `this._fields = {}` plus `_.set(this._fields, key, …)` on user-supplied keys, wired from the new multipart field handler. Parent a1a96a1 only parsed JSON/form/raw via co-body and had no FormFields and no lodash.set of request keys. Later 31a44e4 (2019 TS port) and 43946d1 (v6 rename to src/form_fields.ts, `#fields: any = {}`) are refactors/ports of that same algorithm, not a new first-write.
